calls.head: A shadow job for Hagel, Cirelli and Goncalves
calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Hagel’s line (Hagel, Cirelli and Goncalves) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Senators’ first line is Zetterlund, Stützle and Cozens.

surprises.head: A rough night for Dennis Hildeby
surprises.body: Hildeby allowed 6 goals on 21 shots, worth 3.1 expected goals: 2.9 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 30 starts.

story.head: The Senators run away from the Lightning
paras: Ridly Greig struck first for the Senators early in the first, and Tim Stützle stretched the lead to 2-0 shorthanded midway through the period. Michael Amadio made it 3-0 early in the second. Gage Goncalves and Nick Cousins squared off midway through the period. Stützle scored his second of the night late in the period to make it 4-0 for the Senators. It was a busy third period. Artem Zub and Claude Giroux scored less than two minutes apart early in the period to make it 6-0. Jake Guentzel scored midway through the period and again less than five minutes later to cut Ottawa’s lead to 6-2. Amadio finished with a goal and two assists.
The Senators had the better of the chances. Linus Ullmark made 18 saves for the Sens, and Dennis Hildeby allowed six goals on 21 shots.

Max Crozier took three penalties on his own. He picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Senators improved to 17-7-3, still first in the Atlantic, while the Lightning fell to 15-8-2, slipping to third in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Lightning are on a three-game losing streak.
Jake Guentzel has a point in five straight games.
Artem Zub scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 9 (22 games played since).
NHL.com had projected the Lightning with 12 forwards and six defensemen, but they dressed 11 and seven.
